concepts.def: Having enough food to feed a population.

Factors that reduce the amount of food available to a population. They include: the increasing birth rate, which has threatened food security in some countries; changing diets in developed countries, which means scarce food resources are transported around the world; new pests and pathogens that affect farming; environmental changes that affect food production, such as widespread famine occurring in some countries if rains fail; the cost of agricultural inputs; and conflicts that have arisen in some parts of the world which affect the availability of water or food.
Producing food in ways that can be continued into the future without the supply running out. Sustainable methods must be found to feed all people on Earth.

concepts.term: Restricting energy transfer from food animals
concepts.def: The efficiency of food production can be improved by restricting energy transfer from food animals to the environment. This can be done by limiting their movement and by controlling the temperature of their surroundings, so that more of the energy in their food is used for growth.

concepts.term: High protein foods in animal feed
concepts.def: Some animals are fed high protein foods to increase growth, which improves the efficiency of food production.
Fish stocks in the oceans are declining. It is important to maintain fish stocks at a level where breeding continues, or certain species may disappear altogether in some areas.

concepts.term: Fishing quotas and control of net size
concepts.def: Two methods used to conserve fish stocks at a sustainable level. A fishing quota is a limit on the mass or number of a species that may be caught. Controlling net size, by setting a minimum mesh size, allows young fish to escape so that breeding continues.
Modern biotechnology techniques enable large quantities of microorganisms to be cultured for food, providing a source of protein for a growing human population.
A protein-rich food suitable for vegetarians, produced using the fungus Fusarium. The fungus is grown on glucose syrup, in aerobic conditions, and the biomass is harvested and purified.

concepts.term: Human insulin from a genetically modified bacterium
concepts.def: A genetically modified bacterium produces human insulin. When harvested and purified this is used to treat people with diabetes.

mcqs.q: What is meant by food security?
options: Growing a country's food within its borders.
Storing enough food to survive any famine.
Having enough food to feed a population.
Producing food without damaging habitats.
mcqs.explain: Food security is having enough food to feed a population, which is exactly what this option states.

mcqs.q: A new insect pest spreads into a country and destroys much of its wheat crop. Which biological factor affecting food security does this describe?
options: New pests and pathogens that affect farming.
An increasing birth rate in some countries.
Environmental change such as rains failing.
Changing diets in the developed countries.
mcqs.explain: An insect pest that has newly spread into the country and reduced the harvest is an example of new pests and pathogens that affect farming, one of the biological factors threatening food security.

mcqs.q: A farmer rears animals for meat indoors. Which change would improve the efficiency of food production?
options: Give them more space in which to move around.
Keep them in cool, well ventilated buildings.
Feed them a diet that is lower in protein.
Limit movement and control the temperature.
mcqs.explain: The efficiency of food production can be improved by restricting energy transfer from food animals to the environment, and this is done by limiting their movement and by controlling the temperature of their surroundings.

mcqs.q: Why are some food animals fed high protein foods?
options: To increase their rate of growth.
To give them energy for movement.
To keep their surroundings warmer.
To reduce the food that they eat.
mcqs.explain: Some animals are fed high protein foods to increase growth, which improves the efficiency of food production.

mcqs.q: Fish stocks in one area of ocean are declining. Which action would help to conserve the stocks at a sustainable level?
options: Remove quotas and keep the net size the same.
Use fishing quotas and control the net size.
Use small mesh nets to catch the young fish.
Keep fishing until the stocks begin to fall.
mcqs.explain: Control of net size and the introduction of fishing quotas play important roles in conservation of fish stocks at a sustainable level, maintaining stocks at a level where breeding continues.

mcqs.q: Mycoprotein is a protein-rich food suitable for vegetarians. How is it produced?
options: Bacteria are grown on glucose syrup, in aerobic conditions.
Fusarium is grown on glucose syrup, in anaerobic conditions.
Fusarium is grown on glucose syrup, in aerobic conditions.
Yeast is grown on glucose syrup, in anaerobic conditions.
mcqs.explain: The fungus Fusarium is useful for producing mycoprotein. The fungus is grown on glucose syrup, in aerobic conditions, and the biomass is harvested and purified.

mcqs.q: Golden rice is a genetically modified crop. How can GM crops help to meet the demands of the growing human population?
options: By providing medicines inside the food eaten.
By providing more food, not improved nutrition.
By providing food grown from cultured fungi.
By providing more food or improved nutrition.
mcqs.explain: GM crops could provide more food or food with an improved nutritional value such as golden rice, which is one biotechnical and agricultural solution to the demands of the growing human population.
